newsitem.title: Finland: Insurers lift lively Helsinki to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Insurers lift lively Helsinki to higher close.

text.p: * Shares end up after lively trade as insurers extend gains on hopes for restructuring of the sector and improved profit prospects after recent gains in stocks and bonds.
* Vol FIM 358 million, 28 pct in Nokia
Shares ended a lively session modestly higher on Friday as insurance companies continued to benefit from speculation about a possible shake-up in the sector, brokers said.
"Insurers were also lifted by expectations that recent gains in stocks and bonds would boost their profits," one said.
But brokers said the generally upbeat tone was clouded by Nokia's early losses on Wall Street, which took Nokia 0.10 markka lower to 202.40 after moderate trade in Helsinki.
Pohjola advanced 1.70 markka to 92.80, and Sampo added 6.00 to close at a two year-high 328 markka.
Beverages group Hartwall extended gains following strong January-August profits on Thursday, and it closed active trade 9.00 markka up at 143.00 after touching a new life-high 148.00.
Steel group Rautaruukki ended 0.10 markka lower to 39.50, in what brokers called a mild reaction to the company's profit-warning issued on Friday.
Forestries remained soft. Metsa-Serla, which warned of lower profits on Tuesday, fell 0.50 markka to 29.50.
However, the HEX index closed up 1.5 percent for the week, at its highest since October 2, 1995.
